newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Carter urges Brazil to progress on human rights.
newsitem.headline: Carter urges Brazil to progress on human rights.

text.p: Former U.S. president Jimmy Carter on Wednesday urged Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to press on with his drive to establish respect for human rights in Latin America's largest country, officials said.

Presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral said Carter, visiting Brasilia as part of a Latin American and Caribbean tour, remarked in talks with Cardoso that Brazil still had some way to go on the issue of rights.

"Former president Carter praised what he considered important advances in Brazil in the realm of human rights but observed also that it seemed to him there remained further steps to take," Amaral told reporters.

Cardoso's government is trying to eradicate widespread child and slave labour and curb the notorious impunity of the military police. It has made Brazil one of only a handful of countries to draw up an official National Plan of Human Rights.
Nevertheless, abuses continue, human rights groups say.
Carter, who has passed through Chile and Argentina, is on a five-day visit to Brazil.

The U.S. embassy said Carter was travelling through Latin America to make contact with government leaders ahead of a conference on the region's future. The conference, hosted by the Carter Centre, will take place in Georgia in April.
Carter took part on Wednesday in a round table discussion on human rights and was scheduled to give a news conference on Thursday.

He travels to the Amazonian capital of Manaus on Thursday afternoon where he will take a tour of the rain forest. The former U.S. leader heads for Jamaica on Saturday on the last leg of his Latin American tour.
